intelligence.enrichment: Soluble sugar particles can become distributed in the spaces between water particles, so the water level may decrease after dissolving; insoluble sand does not dissolve, settles down, occupies space, and increases the total volume. solute particles fitting into interparticle spaces versus insoluble particles settling -> different visible level and volume changes The learner compares soluble sugar with insoluble sand: dissolved sugar particles occupy spaces between water particles and may lower the level after mark B, while sand settles, occupies space, and increases total volume. All small solids added to water behave the same once they are stirred.
